diagrams.title: Dermatomyositis Autoantibody Phenotypes
diagrams.subtitle: Use phenotype concordance; commercial assays are not perfectly standardized

children.name: MDA5
children.detail: Clinically amyopathic or less-muscular phenotype; painful palmar papules, ulcers/necrosis, oral disease, arthritis; high ILD and rapidly progressive ILD risk.

children.name: TIF1γ
children.detail: Often extensive or atypical cutaneous disease; strong adult malignancy association. Lower frequency of ILD than several other phenotypes.

children.name: NXP2
children.detail: Severe muscle disease, dysphagia, myalgia, edema, calcinosis; adult malignancy association in some cohorts. Juvenile disease commonly has calcinosis.

children.name: Mi-2
children.detail: Classic Gottron/heliotrope/shawl phenotype with prominent skin and muscle disease; often treatment-responsive and lower ILD risk.

children.name: SAE
children.detail: Skin-predominant onset may precede myositis; dysphagia can be prominent. Associations vary by cohort.

children.name: Antisynthetase antibodies
children.detail: ILD, inflammatory arthritis, Raynaud, fever, myositis, and mechanic’s hands; the complete syndrome need not be present.

children.name: PM/Scl, Ku, U1-RNP, Ro52 and other associated antibodies
children.detail: Suggest overlap myositis or modify organ risk; Ro52 may accompany antisynthetase disease and correlate with ILD severity in some cohorts.

root.name: Myositis-specific / associated autoantibodies
root.detail: Autoantibodies support prognosis and organ-risk assessment; they are not required for diagnosis and should not overrule the phenotype.

diagrams.title: Cancer Screening in Adult IIM / Dermatomyositis
diagrams.subtitle: Operationalized from the IMACS international guideline; use local pathways and shared decision-making

steps.prompt: Adult-onset IIM with cancer risk assessment completed?
steps.detail: First complete standard age- and sex-appropriate population screening and evaluate any symptoms or examination findings that independently require diagnostic workup.

steps.prompt: Identify IMACS high- and intermediate-risk factors
steps.detail: **High-risk examples:** dermatomyositis subtype, anti-TIF1γ, anti-NXP2, age >40 years at onset, persistent high disease activity despite therapy, moderate/severe dysphagia, cutaneous necrosis/ulceration. **Intermediate examples:** clinically amyopathic DM, selected antibodies such as MDA5/SAE1, male sex, and other guideline-defined factors.

steps.prompt: 1 high-risk factor OR at least 2 intermediate-risk factors?
High risk: basic + enhanced screening at diagnosis
steps.detail: Basic screening includes history, examination, CBC, liver profile, inflammatory markers, serum protein electrophoresis, urinalysis, and chest radiograph per guideline. Enhanced screening includes CT neck/chest/abdomen/pelvis plus sex-specific and GI testing as appropriate.

steps.prompt: Repeat basic screening annually for 3 years; consider additional testing if initial evaluation is negative
steps.detail: Depending on local expertise and patient factors, consider FDG-PET/CT, upper/lower GI endoscopy, or nasoendoscopy for patients from regions with high nasopharyngeal carcinoma incidence. New symptoms always override the schedule.

steps.prompt: Moderate risk: basic + enhanced screening once at diagnosis
steps.detail: Continue routine population screening and symptom-directed evaluation thereafter unless risk or phenotype changes.

steps.prompt: Standard risk: basic screening at diagnosis
steps.detail: Continue routine population screening. Do not infer zero risk; investigate any concerning symptom, sign, or laboratory abnormality.

citations.quote: IMACS international guideline provides risk-stratified cancer screening recommendations for idiopathic inflammatory myopathies.

steps.prompt: New dermatomyositis / idiopathic inflammatory myopathy diagnosis?
High ILD-risk phenotype or respiratory concern?
steps.detail: High-risk clues include anti-MDA5 or antisynthetase antibodies, mechanic’s hands, inflammatory arthritis, Raynaud, palmar papules, ulcers/necrosis, unexplained cough/dyspnea, crackles, or reduced oxygenation.

steps.prompt: Obtain baseline PFTs; decide on HRCT using risk, guideline framework, and local practice
steps.detail: A normal chest radiograph does not exclude ILD. A cancer-staging CT is not a substitute for HRCT when ILD characterization is needed.

steps.prompt: Obtain PFTs and HRCT promptly—evidence of ILD or rapid progression?
New/worsening cough, dyspnea, exertional desaturation, chest symptoms, or falling PFTs?
Coordinate rheumatology, pulmonology, radiology, and dermatology
steps.detail: Characterize pattern/extent, exclude infection and alternative causes, document baseline PFTs/oxygenation, and choose treatment based on phenotype, severity, trajectory, and comorbidity.

steps.prompt: Treat as rapidly progressive ILD / respiratory emergency
steps.detail: Hospitalize when appropriate; urgently exclude infection and pulmonary embolism; initiate specialist-directed combination immunomodulation and supportive care. MDA5-associated RP-ILD can deteriorate quickly.

steps.prompt: Serial clinical review and PFT monitoring
steps.detail: Repeat PFTs at intervals matched to risk and recent trajectory; obtain HRCT when symptoms, PFTs, or clinical concern indicate. Do not use symptoms alone to declare stability.
